title: Idli
steps: Soak rice and urad dal (with fenugreek if using) separately for 4–6 hours. Grind urad dal to a fluffy batter and rice to a slightly coarse batter. Mix, add salt and ferment overnight or 8–12 hours.
Grease idli moulds. Pour batter into moulds and steam for 10–12 minutes till a toothpick comes out clean.
Serve hot with sambar, coconut chutney and milagai podi mixed with oil/ghee.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Soft, spongy texture comes from proper fermentation and grinding.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A healthy, oil-free steamed breakfast staple across Tamil Nadu.

title: Ven Pongal
steps: Dry-roast moong dal lightly. Pressure-cook rice and moong dal together with enough water till soft and mushy.
In ghee, temper cumin, peppercorns, cashews, ginger, green chillies and curry leaves.
Pour the tempering over the cooked rice-dal mixture. Mix well, adjust salt and consistency with hot water if needed.
Serve hot with sambar and coconut chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Ginger, green chillies, curry leaves, cashews

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Also called Khara Pongal. Generous ghee and whole pepper-cumin are essential.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Festival and everyday comfort breakfast.

title: Masala Dosa
steps: Prepare or use well-fermented dosa batter of pouring consistency.
For potato masala: Boil and mash potatoes. Temper mustard, curry leaves, green chillies and onion; add turmeric and salt. Mix with potatoes.
Heat a tawa, pour and spread batter into a thin circle. Drizzle oil/ghee. Place potato filling in the centre, fold and roast till crisp.
Serve hot with sambar and coconut chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chillies, curry leaves, mustard, turmeric

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Crispy exterior and soft spiced potato filling define a good masala dosa.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A global ambassador of Tamil / South Indian breakfast.

title: Adai
steps: Soak rice and dals for 3–4 hours. Grind coarsely with red chilli and fennel (do not make a fine batter). Add salt.
Mix in finely chopped onion, green chillies, curry leaves and coriander.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of thick batter and spread into a thick circle. Drizzle oil and cook on both sides till golden and crisp.
Serve with avocado chutney, jaggery or any spicy chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Rice + mixed dals (chana, toor, urad, moong)
Onion, green chillies, curry leaves, coriander

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Protein-rich thicker cousin of dosa, popular in Tamil Nadu households.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Coarse texture is characteristic.

title: Sambar
steps: Pressure-cook toor dal till soft. Extract tamarind pulp.
Cook vegetables in tamarind water with turmeric and salt till tender. Add sambar powder and cooked dal. Simmer.
Temper mustard, fenugreek, dry red chilli, curry leaves and hing in oil/ghee. Pour over the sambar.
Serve with rice, idli, dosa or vada.

fullIngredients.name: Mixed vegetables (drumstick, brinjal, pumpkin, shallots, tomato)
Mustard, fenugreek, dry red chilli, curry leaves, asafoetida

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The balance of tamarind sourness, dal body and fresh ground spices is key.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Arachuvitta sambar (freshly ground spices) is preferred in many Tamil homes.

title: Rasam
steps: Extract tamarind water. Cook with tomato, rasam powder/crushed spices, salt and a little turmeric till the raw smell disappears.
Add crushed garlic if using and simmer briefly. Do not boil vigorously after this stage.
Temper mustard, dry red chilli, curry leaves and hing. Pour over the rasam. Finish with coriander leaves.
Serve with rice or as a light soup.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Thinner and more aromatic than sambar; often the second course in a Tamil meal.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Pepper-cumin rasam and tomato rasam are everyday favourites.

title: Puliyodarai (Tamarind Rice)
steps: Heat sesame oil, temper mustard, dals, peanuts, dry red chilli, fenugreek and curry leaves. Add turmeric, hing, tamarind extract, salt and a little jaggery. Cook till the mixture thickens and oil separates (pulikachal).
Mix the spice paste thoroughly with cooled cooked rice.
Rest for some time so flavours absorb. Serve with appalam and yogurt.

fullIngredients.name: Sesame oil, mustard, chana dal, urad dal, peanuts, dry red chilli, curry leaves, fenugreek

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Temple-style and travel-friendly rice; tastes better after a few hours.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Sesame oil is traditional and gives authentic aroma.

title: Chettinad Chicken
steps: Dry-roast and grind the whole spices to make fresh Chettinad masala.
Heat oil, sauté onion, curry leaves and ginger-garlic. Add tomato and the ground masala. Cook till oil separates.
Add chicken, salt and a little water. Cover and cook till tender and the gravy is thick and aromatic.
Finish with crushed pepper if desired. Serve with rice, dosa, appam or parotta.

fullIngredients.name: Chettinad spice mix (fennel, pepper, coriander, cinnamon, star anise, kalpasi, red chilli)

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Freshly ground spices and kalpasi (stone flower) give the distinctive Chettinad flavour.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: One of the most famous non-vegetarian dishes from Tamil Nadu.

title: Thayir Sadam (Curd Rice)
steps: Mash the cooked rice lightly while still warm. Mix with curd, a little milk and salt till creamy.
Temper mustard, urad dal, green chilli, ginger, curry leaves and hing in oil/ghee. Pour over the rice.
Mix well and garnish with coriander and optional fruits.
Serve chilled or at room temperature with pickle and appalam.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard, urad dal, green chilli, ginger, curry leaves, asafoetida

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The classic cooling finisher of a Tamil meal.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best made with slightly overcooked soft rice.

title: Medu Vada
steps: Soak urad dal for 3–4 hours. Drain and grind to a smooth, fluffy batter with minimal water. Add salt, green chillies, ginger, curry leaves, pepper and cumin. Mix well (add onion if using).
Wet hands, shape into doughnut-like rings and slide into hot oil. Fry on medium heat till golden and crisp outside, soft inside.
Serve hot with sambar and coconut chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Green chillies, ginger, curry leaves, black pepper, cumin

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Fluffy batter and medium-hot oil are key to soft interiors.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Classic accompaniment to idli in a tiffin platter.

title: Murukku
steps: Mix rice flour, urad flour, spices, salt and melted butter/oil. Add water to form a soft, non-sticky dough.
Load into a murukku press with star or spiral plate. Extrude into hot oil in circular shapes.
Fry on medium heat till golden and crisp. Drain and cool completely.
Store in airtight containers.

fullIngredients.name: Butter or oil, cumin, sesame, asafoetida, chilli powder

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: A quintessential Tamil snack for festivals and tea-time.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Dough consistency determines crispness.

title: Kuzhi Paniyaram
steps: Temper mustard, urad dal, curry leaves, green chillies and onion. Mix into the idli/dosa batter along with coriander.
Heat a kuzhi paniyaram pan, add a few drops of oil in each cavity. Pour batter to fill three-quarters.
Cover and cook till the bottom is golden, flip and cook the other side.
Serve hot with coconut chutney or sambar.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chillies, curry leaves, coriander

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Excellent way to use leftover batter. Soft and slightly crisp.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Popular in Chettinad and across Tamil Nadu.

title: Beans Poriyal (or Mixed Vegetable Poriyal)
steps: Temper mustard, urad dal, dry red chilli and curry leaves in oil. Add the chopped vegetable, turmeric and salt.
Sprinkle a little water, cover and cook till tender but still bright.
Add grated coconut, mix well and cook for another minute.
Serve as a dry side with rice, sambar and rasam.

fullIngredients.name: Beans or any vegetable (cabbage, carrot, beans)
Mustard, urad dal, dry red chilli, curry leaves

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Poriyal is the everyday dry vegetable side in a Tamil meal.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Coconut is added at the end for freshness.

title: Meen Kuzhambu (Fish Curry)
steps: Extract tamarind water. Lightly marinate fish with turmeric and salt.
Heat oil, temper mustard, fenugreek and curry leaves. Sauté shallots, garlic and tomato. Add spice powders and tamarind water. Bring to a boil.
Gently add fish pieces and simmer on low heat till cooked (do not over-stir).
Rest for some time before serving. Serve with rice.

fullIngredients.name: Red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric, fenugreek
Sesame oil or gingelly oil, mustard, curry leaves

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Coastal Tamil Nadu style uses gingelly oil and tamarind for the characteristic tang.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best made a few hours ahead so flavours develop.
